title: Ars Notoria sive Flores Aurei
shelf_note: A two-column Gothic manuscript of the Ars Notoria: the Latin prayers, the nomina barbara and the hour prologues match the title. Tradition and collections are empty, so there is no shelf to test against.
rights_flag: The scan has a burned-in footer reading "Copyright © Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana / powered by AMLAD·NTT DATA" and a diagonal watermark across the text reading "ALL RIGHTS RESERVED © Biblioteca Apostolica". The text itself is medieval, but the image carries a holder's rights claim.
structure_note: The structure counts give pages_translated 0, but the book field gives 70: the counts disagree. Only 19 of 72 pages have a printed number, and 5 of those step backwards. The folio numbers on this leaf are faint pencil/ink in the corner, so the backsteps are most likely misread numerals rather than a broken sequence. One page cannot settle that.

pages.layout: two ruled columns, red rubrics, a long block of nomina barbara in the left column; a strip of the facing leaf at the left edge; Vatican copyright banner at the foot and a watermark over the text

ocr_errors.problem: The red rubric at the top of the right column introduces the later prologue of the FIFTH prayer. The OCR turns it into a 'first prologue of the sixth hour', so the page shows two sixth-hour headings and the section is mislabelled.

missing.english: Here begins the fifth prayer, which is of the sacred particles
missing.why: 'Sacred particles' is opaque. A reader needs to know what the rubric's 'particulae' are: the divisions of the Ars Notoria's prayer sequence.

missing.english: the prologue of the first prayer of the sixth hour
missing.why: The 'hours' (horae) are the Notory Art's ritual sequence of prayers, not liturgical hours, and nothing tells the reader this.

book_verdict: The Ars Notoria leaf is the right page and the translation is broadly faithful. However, the OCR misreads a rubric ('posterior prologue of the fifth prayer' becomes 'first prologue of the sixth hour'), so two identical sixth-hour headings appear and the section is mislabelled. Several abbreviated lines are garbled, and the scan carries a Vatican 'All rights reserved' watermark.
